invariants: HTTP status carries transport semantics while stable error_code or result_code carries business semantics
HTTP 202 means accepted and never final success
parameter, permission, revision, idempotency, state transition, quota, authority and projection failures remain distinguishable
trace_id and operation_id correlate the API result with logs, metrics and business audit without exposing a stack
unknown failures return a safe message and a searchable trace rather than a successful toast
domain.compensation: preserve the failed terminal result and dispatch only the compensation registered for the stable action_id

data.migration: no common schema mutation; each business command persists minimal audit and outbox in its owning PostgreSQL transaction

negative_tests: permission denial cannot be rewritten as HTTP 200 or a successful business result
error details and logs cannot expose stack traces, credentials or another tenant identifier
a stale revision returns current_revision without mutating the aggregate

stop_conditions: error/result identity diverges across HTTP, job state, audit or authoritative data

tests: G0 error catalog OpenAPI and generated TypeScript shape
G1 common response helper mapping and secret-safe error tests
G2 real P0 query and command failure injection
G3 HTTP job authoritative data audit and outbox reconciliation
G5 Windows Chrome accepted partial failed and compensated states
G6 gateway preserves upstream status and rollback
evidence: one trace proves the same code, operation, revision and final result across browser, HTTP, job, PG, audit and projection status
